subject: history_social
passage: The edicts of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, carved on rocks and pillars across the Indian subcontinent in the third century BCE, became unreadable for centuries after the Brahmi script in which most of them were written fell out of use. Their decipherment in the 1830s drew on several kinds of evidence: coins that gave the same royal names in both Greek and Brahmi; short donor inscriptions from the stupa at ______ of which ended with the same two characters; and painstaking comparisons of letter shapes across hundreds of copied texts.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The colon introduces a list of three items separated by semicolons. The blank falls inside the second item, "short donor inscriptions from the stupa at Sanchi, many of which ended with the same two characters." Within that item, "many of which ..." is a nonessential clause about the inscriptions, so a comma, not a semicolon, sets it off.
explanation.A: Correct. The comma sets off the nonessential clause "many of which ended with the same two characters" inside the second item of the list.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The other semicolons make one tempting, but a semicolon here would split the second item in two, leaving "many of which ended with the same two characters" as a separate "item" that names no kind of evidence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon can't be used inside a list item to introduce a relative clause, and the sentence already uses a colon to introduce the list.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A nonessential clause beginning "many of which" must be set off with a comma; without one, the sentence seems to mention "Sanchi many."
